title: Amid Legal Battles Suno Says It Will Start Watermarking Songs
report:
Here is a 4-sentence summary and 5 key facts about Suno's new tools and lawsuits:

**Summary:** Suno, an AI-generated song creation platform, has introduced new tools to prevent misuse of its tracks on other streaming platforms and update community guidelines to prohibit copycat songs. The changes come as the company faces numerous lawsuits from labels and artist bodies over copyright infringement concerns. Suno will use audio watermarking and fingerprinting to mark tracks made on its platform and limit downloads to prevent mass distribution on streaming platforms. The startup aims to promote original creation while enabling more people to make music with its AI tools.

**Key Facts:**

1. **Lawsuits:** Suno is facing lawsuits from Universal Music Group (UMG), Sony Music Group, and the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) over copyright infringement concerns.
2. **Audio watermarking:** Suno will use audio watermarking and fingerprinting to mark tracks made on its platform and prevent misuse on other streaming platforms.
3. **Community guidelines:** The company has updated its community guidelines to explicitly prohibit "deceptive audio presented as real" and "using a real person's voice or likeness without permission".
4. **Copyright detection:** Suno has signed an agreement with lyrics provider Musixmatch to use its Sentinel system for copyright detection.
5. **Data breach:** A data breach in November 2025 revealed that the platform scraped YouTube, Deezer, and Genius to train its models, affecting 55 million users and leading to a class action lawsuit in Massachusetts.

title: House Affordable Housing Bill Trump
report:
**Summary (4 sentences)**
The US House has voted in favor of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a bipartisan bill aimed at making housing more affordable and limiting institutional investors' role in the market. The legislation will now go to President Donald Trump's desk for signature, with lawmakers from both parties eager to campaign on it ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. The bill aims to address the housing affordability problem by reducing regulations and capping the number of single-family homes institutional investors can buy at 350. Despite some opposition from conservative hardliners who wanted a voter-ID bill included, the measure passed with overwhelming support.

**Key Facts (5)**

1. **Voting results**: The House voted in favor of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act by a margin of 358-32.
2. **Bipartisan support**: The legislation received rare bipartisan support, passing out of the Senate on Monday night with an 85-5 vote.
3. **Key provisions**: The bill aims to reduce regulations, limit institutional investors' role in the housing market, and cap the number of single-family homes they can buy at 350.
4. **Campaigning ahead of midterms**: Both Democrats and Republicans plan to campaign on the legislation ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, as affordability is a top concern for voters.
5. **Controversy over voter-ID bill**: Some conservative hardliners opposed the housing measure because it did not include a voter-ID bill known as the SAVE America Act, which requires ID at the ballot box and proof of citizenship to register for elections.

title: Ea Sports Ufc 6 Leads Game Sales For June A Month Where Spending Fell 21 Compared To
report:
**Summary (4 sentences)**
According to a report by Circana, U.S. video game spending in June dropped 21% compared to last year, due in part to the record-breaking launch of the Nintendo Switch 2 in June 2025. Despite this decline, EA Sports UFC 6 led game sales for June, followed closely by Meccha Chameleon and 007 First Light. The top 10 best-selling games list also included Star Fox, Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight, and Minecraft. Overall, video game spending reached $4.5 billion in June, with first-half spending down 1% compared to last year.

**Key Facts (5)**

1. **EA Sports UFC 6 leads game sales**: EA Sports UFC 6 was the top-selling game for June, followed by Meccha Chameleon and 007 First Light.
2. **Video game spending drops 21%**: U.S. video game spending in June dropped 21% compared to last year, due to a strong June 2025 bolstered by the Nintendo Switch 2 launch.
3. **Switch 2 hardware sales decline**: Switch 2 hardware spending dropped 79% compared to its launch month last year, while PlayStation 5 spending fell 19% and Xbox Series spending fell more than double that.
4. **Subscription services experience growth**: Subscription service spending was the only content segment to experience growth in June, jumping up 7% compared to last year.
5. **Decline in accessories spending**: June accessories spending fell 21% from last year, with controller spending specifically dropping 31%.
